## A printer's view of slides

::: {.lead style="max-width: 24em;"}
[T]{.dropcap}he page is patient. Type set on a generous measure, with air around it, gives the reader room to think. Slides can borrow that calm.
:::

## What goes in this issue

- A note on typography
- Two columns of evidence
- A picture and its caption
- One quotation worth keeping
- A short passage of code
- A closing remark

[Read in sequence; each follows from the last.]{.footnote-inline}

## Two columns

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
### The case for restraint
Strip the slide. Remove the second adjective. Trust the reader to follow a clear sentence without ornament.
:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
### The risk of restraint
Stripped too far, the slide becomes a label. Without verbs and examples, the argument cannot land.
:::
::::

## A passage of code

```r
library(dplyr)
penguins |>
  filter(!is.na(bill_length_mm)) |>
  group_by(species) |>
  summarise(mean_bill = mean(bill_length_mm), n = n())
```

[A small example in R, set in the same measure as the body.]{.footnote-inline}
